claim: GPCRs are the target of about 35% of approved drugs
source: The structural basis for the pharmacology of human G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), the most abundant membrane proteins and the target of about 35% of approved drugs, is still a matter of intense study.
evidence: This is a widely cited statistic in the GPCR field, supported by citation in the manuscript.

claim: mwSuMD can address complex binding processes intrinsically linked to protein dynamics out of reach of classic MD
source: We demonstrate that mwSuMD can address complex binding processes intrinsically linked to protein dynamics out of reach of classic MD.
evidence: This claim is supported by the simulations and results presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: This is the first time the whole sequence of events leading from an inactive GPCR to the GDP release is simulated without any energy bias
source: To our knowledge, this is the first time the whole sequence of events leading from an inactive GPCR to the GDP release is simulated without any energy bias.
evidence: The authors explicitly state this is a novel achievement based on their simulations.

claim: Vertebrate GPCRs are subdivided into five subfamilies according to function and sequence
source: Vertebrate GPCRs are subdivided into five subfamilies (Rhodopsin or class A, Secretin or class B, Glutamate or class C, Adhesion, and Frizzled/Taste2) according to function and sequence (Schiöth and Fredriksson, 2005; G protein-coupled receptors, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established classification systems.

claim: GPCRs possess seven transmembrane helices connected by three extracellular loops and three intracellular loops
source: X-ray and cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) show that GPCRs possess seven transmembrane (TM) helices connected by three extracellular loops (ECLs) and three intracellular loops (ICLs), with an extended and structured N-terminal extracellular domain (ECD) in all subtypes, but class A.
evidence: This structural description is supported by X-ray and cryo-EM data cited in the manuscript.

claim: The primary function of GPCRs is transducing extracellular chemical signals into the cytosol by binding and activating four G protein families
source: The primary function of GPCRs is transducing extracellular chemical signals into the cytosol by binding and activating four G protein families (Gs/olf, Gi/o, G12/13, and Gq/11) responsible for decreasing (Gi/o) or increasing (Gs/olf) cyclic adenosine-3',5'-monophosphate, and generating inositol-1,4,5-triphosphate and diacylglycerol to increase Ca2+ intracellular levels (Gq) (Syrovatkina et al., 2016).
evidence: This functional description is supported by citation to established GPCR signaling mechanisms.

claim: Classic MD sampling is limited to the microsecond or, in the best conditions, the millisecond time scale
source: However, classic MD sampling is limited to the microsecond or, in the best conditions, the millisecond time scale (Hollingsworth and Dror, 2018; Durrant and McCammon, 2011).
evidence: This limitation is supported by citations to literature on MD timescales.

claim: Metadynamics, accelerated MD, and Gaussian-accelerated MD introduce an energy potential to overcome energy barriers
source: Among the most popular and effective ones are metadynamics (Bussi and Laio, 2020) and path collective variables metadynamics (D'Amore et al., 2024), accelerated MD (aMD) (Hamelberg et al., 2004), and Gaussian-accelerated MD (GaMD) (Miao et al., 2015), which introduce an energy potential to overcome the energy barriers preventing the complete exploration of the free energy surface, thus de facto bias the simulation.
evidence: This characterization of biased MD methods is supported by citations to the respective methodologies.

claim: SuMD is an energetically unbiased MD protocol
source: Energetically unbiased MD protocols, on the other hand, comprise weighted ensemble MD (Zuckerman and Chong, 2017), swarms approach (Fleetwood et al., 2020), AdaptiveGoal (Lovera et al., 2019), and SuMD (Cuzzolin et al., 2016; Sabbadin and Moro, 2014), which have largely been applied to (unbinding) small molecules, peptides, and small proteins (Cuzzolin et al., 2016; Sabbadin and Moro, 2014; Deganutti et al., 2021a; Dong et al., 2020; Deganutti et al., 2021c; Cary et al., 2022).
evidence: This classification is supported by citations to the SuMD methodology and related unbiased methods.

claim: mwSuMD was designed to address more complex conformational transitions and protein-protein associations
source: Since SuMD is optimized for (un)bindings, we have designed mwSuMD to address more complex conformational transitions and protein-protein associations.
evidence: This is the stated purpose of the method development.

claim: GPCRs preferentially couple to very few G proteins out of 23 possible counterparts
source: GPCRs preferentially couple to very few G proteins out of 23 possible counterparts (Flock et al., 2017; Wall et al., 2022).
evidence: This selectivity is supported by citations to studies on G protein coupling.

claim: Dynamic and transient interactions determine whether the encounter between a GPCR and a G protein results in productive or unproductive coupling
source: It is increasingly accepted that dynamic and transient interactions determine whether the encounter between a GPCR and a G protein results in productive or unproductive coupling (Culhane et al., 2022).
evidence: This mechanistic understanding is supported by citation to recent work.

claim: AVP is an endogenous hormone that mediates antidiuretic effects on the kidney by signaling through three class A GPCR subtypes
source: AVP is an endogenous hormone (Figure 1a) that mediates antidiuretic effects on the kidney by signaling through three class A GPCR subtypes: V1a and V1b receptors activate phospholipases via Gq/11, while the V2R activates adenylyl cyclase by interacting with Gs (Birnbaumer, 2000) and is a therapeutic target for hyponatremia, hypertension, and incontinence (Ball, 2007).
evidence: This functional description is supported by citations to AVP pharmacology.

claim: The average AVP RMSD during a classic MD simulation of the X-ray AVP:V2R complex was 3.80±0.52 Å
source: As a reference, the AVP root mean square deviation (RMSD) during a classic (unsupervised) equilibrium MD simulation of the X-ray AVP:V2R complex was 3.80±0.52 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the simulation data presented in the figure.

claim: SuMD produced a minimum RMSD to the cryo-EM complex of 4.28 Å for AVP binding to V2R
source: SuMD (Cuzzolin et al., 2016; Sabbadin and Moro, 2014) produced a minimum RMSD to the cryo-EM complex of 4.28 Å, with most of the replicas (i.e. distribution's mode) having an RMSD close to 10 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: This is a direct result from the SuMD simulations reported in the figure.

claim: Decreasing the time window duration from 600 ps to 100 ps impaired the SuMD ability to predict the experimental complex
source: Interestingly, decreasing the time window duration from 600 ps to 100 ps impaired the SuMD ability to predict the experimental complex (Figure 1a), but enhanced mwSuMD accuracy and precision (Figure 1b–d).
evidence: This comparison is based on the simulation results shown in the figures.

claim: The combination of RMSD as the supervised metric and SMscore produced the best results for AVP binding with minimum RMSD of 3.85 Å and distribution mode RMSD of 4.40 Å
source: The combination of RMSD as the supervised metric and SMscore produced the best results in terms of minimum RMSD and distribution mode RMSD, 3.85 Å and 4.40 Å, respectively (Figure 1d, Video 1), in agreement with the AVP deviations in the equilibrium MD simulation of the X-ray AVP:V2R complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct result from the mwSuMD simulations with specific settings.

claim: mwSuMD pinpointed V2R residues E184ECL2, P298ECL3, and E303ECL3 as involved during AVP binding
source: For example, mwSuMD pinpointed V2R residues E184ECL2, P298ECL3, and E303ECL3 (Figure 2a) as involved during AVP binding, although not in contact with the ligand in the orthosteric complex.
evidence: This is an observation from the mwSuMD simulation trajectories.

claim: None of the residues E184ECL2, P298ECL3, and E303ECL3 are yet characterized through mutagenesis studies according to the GPCRdb
source: None of them are yet characterized through mutagenesis studies according to the GPCRdb (Isberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on a database query cited in the manuscript.

claim: mwSuMD outperformed SuMD in terms of time required to complete AVP dissociation from V2R
source: Overall, mwSuMD outperformed SuMD in terms of time required to complete a dissociation (Figure 2c, Video 2), producing dissociation paths almost 10 times faster than SuMD.
evidence: This is a direct comparison of simulation times from the data presented.

claim: ECL2 and ECL3 were slightly more involved during AVP association than dissociation
source: Here, the V2R residues involved during the dissociation were comparable to the binding (Figure 2a and b), although ECL2 and ECL3 were slightly more involved during the association than the dissociation, in analogy with other class A and B GPCRs (Dong et al., 2020; Deganutti et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing binding and unbinding simulations, supported by citations to similar findings.

claim: In the inactive GLP-1R, residues forming the binding site for PF06882961 are dislocated and scattered due to structural reorganization of the TMD and ECD
source: In the inactive GLP-1R, residues forming the binding site for the non-peptide agonist PF06882961 are dislocated and scattered due to the structural reorganization of the transmembrane domain (TMD) and ECD (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a) that occurs on activation.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing inactive and active structures.

claim: GLP-1R in complex with GLP-1 or different agonists present distinct structural features, even among structurally related ligands
source: Moreover, GLP-1R in complex with GLP-1 or different agonists present distinct structural features, even among structurally related ligands (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b and c).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing different GLP-1R structures.

claim: mwSuMD simulated the binding of PF06882961 reaching an RMSD to its bound conformation in 7LCJ of 3.79±0.83 Å
source: We simulated the binding of PF06882961, reaching an RMSD to its bound conformation in 7LCJ of 3.79±0.83 Å (computed on the second half of the merged trajectory, superimposing on GLP-1R Cα atoms of TMD residues 150–390), using multistep supervision on different system metrics (Figure 3) to model the structural hallmark of GLP-1R activation (Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a direct result from the mwSuMD simulation.

claim: The mwSuMD simulation sampled a counterclockwise helix rotation of TM6 consistent with GLP-1R cryo-EM structures in the active, Gs-coupled state
source: Interestingly, the mwSuMD simulation during stage 4 (TM6 supervision) sampled a counterclockwise helix rotation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a) consistent with the GLP-1R cryo-EM structures in the active, Gs-coupled state (Zhang et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an observation from the simulation data compared to experimental structures.

claim: The central polar network is pivotal for mediating GLP-1 signaling
source: A more detailed analysis revealed that the central polar network, which is pivotal for mediating GLP-1 signaling (Wootten et al., 2016), and the residues at the TM6 kink level adopted active-like conformations during the final stage of the simulation (Figure 4a).
evidence: This functional importance is supported by citation, and the conformational change is observed in the simulation.

claim: During two out of three replicas of β2 AR:Gs binding, both Gα and Gβ achieved distance values close to 5 Å with minimum RMSD of 3.94 Å and 3.96 Å respectively
source: During two out of three replicas, both Gα and Gβ achieved distance values close to 5 Å (minimum RMSD = 3.94 Å and 3.96 Å respectively), in good agreement with the reference (the β2 AR:Gs complex, PDB 3SN6, Figure 5—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a direct result from the mwSuMD simulations of β2 AR:Gs binding.

claim: G proteins bear potential palmitoylation and myristoylation sites that anchor the inactive trimer to the plasma membrane
source: A possible pitfall is that G proteins bear potential palmitoylation and myristoylation sites that anchor the inactive trimer to the plasma membrane (Linder et al., 1993; Zhang et al., 2004), de facto restraining possible binding paths to the receptor.
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on G protein lipidation.

claim: In about 50 ns of mwSuMD, the Giα subunit engaged its intracellular binding site on A1R and formed a complex in good agreement with the cryo-EM structure with RMSD ≈ 5 Å
source: In about 50 ns of mwSuMD, the Giα subunit engaged its intracellular binding site on A1R and formed a complex in good agreement with the cryo-EM structure (PDB 6D9H, RMSD ≈ 5 Å).
evidence: This is a direct result from the mwSuMD simulation of A1R:Gi binding.

claim: 1 μs of classic MD did not produce a productive engagement of Gi with A1R as the Giα remained at RMSD values >40 Å
source: For comparison, 1 μs of cMD did not produce a productive engagement as the Giα remained at RMSD values >40 Å (Figure 5—figure supplement 1d), suggesting the effectiveness of mwSuMD in sampling G protein binding rare events without the input of energy.
evidence: This is a direct comparison between classic MD and mwSuMD results.

claim: All three mwSuMD replicas of Gs binding to GLP-1R showed the Gs approaching GLP-1R, with two out of three reaching an RMSD of the Gsα subunit close to or less than 10 Å
source: All three mwSuMD replicas showed the Gs approaching GLP-1R, with two out of three reaching an RMSD of the Gsα subunit close to or less than 10 Å, compared to the experimental complex 7LCI (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is a direct result from the mwSuMD simulations of Gs binding to GLP-1R.

claim: Replica 2 of Gs binding to GLP-1R reproduced the cryo-EM GLP-1R:Gs complex with RMSD values of 7.59±1.58 Å, 12.15±2.13 Å, and 13.73±2.24 Å for Gα, Gβ, and Gγ, respectively
source: Replica 2, in particular, reproduced the cryo-EM GLP-1R:Gs complex with RMSD values to 7LCI of 7.59±1.58 Å, 12.15±2.13 Å, and 13.73±2.24 Å for Gα, Gβ, and Gγ, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the simulation data.

claim: PF06882961 and GDP were respectively stabilized and destabilized during the simulated Gs association
source: According to the model of G protein activation, the G protein binding has the effect of allosterically stabilizing the orthosteric agonist in complex with the receptor (Deganutti et al., 2022) and destabilizing the GDP bound to Gα, triggering its release and exchange with guanosine triphosphate (Gregorio et al., 2017), upon opening of the G protein alpha-helical domain (AHD). Following this model, PF06882961 and GDP were respectively stabilized and destabilized during the simulated Gs association (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b and c).
evidence: This is an observation from the simulation data that supports a cited model.

claim: The interaction between D3446.33 and R385α5 is proposed to be important for Gs coupling
source: The analysis of atomic contacts along the binding path of Gs to GLP-1R highlights a few persistent interactions not observed in the equilibrium MD simulations of GLP-1R:Gs cryo-EM complexes Deganutti et al., 2022; e.g., we propose the hidden interaction between D3446.33 and R385α5 to be important for Gs coupling (Appendix 1—table 1), which would explain the GLP-1 EC50 reduction upon mutation of position 344 to Ala (Yuan et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on simulation observations and supported by cited mutagenesis data.

claim: mwSuMD suggested several structural changes as implicated in GDP dissociation including AHD opening, conformational change of αG-α4 loop, and rupture of the hydrogen bond between GDP and D295Gα
source: mwSuMD suggested several structural changes as implicated in GDP dissociation (Figure 5f–h): (i) the AHD opening; (ii) the conformational change of αG-α4 loop (residues A303Gα-P332Gα), in concert with a loosening of interactions between D323Gα and K3426.31, and (iii) the rupture of the hydrogen bond between GDP and D295Gα triggered by the movement of αG away from the GDP binding site (Figure 5f).
evidence: These are observations from the mwSuMD simulation of GDP dissociation.

claim: The involvement of αG through the αG-α4 during the release of GDP from Gs is supported by hydrogen/deuterium exchange experiments
source: The involvement of αG through the αG-α4 during the release of GDP from Gs is supported by hydrogen/deuterium exchange experiments (Du et al., 2019), while the role of D275Gα has been probed with functional assays on the Gi isoform mutant D272GαiA (Ham et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: A similar αG behavior was recently suggested by MD simulations of the Gs binding pathway to β2 AR
source: Moreover, a similar αG behavior was recently suggested by MD simulations of the Gs binding pathway to β2 AR (Batebi et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a recent simulation study.

claim: The αG-α4 loop length and amino acidic composition diverge among G protein isoforms, suggesting a role in G protein selectivity
source: We also note that the αG-α4 loop length and amino acidic composition diverge among G protein isoforms, further suggesting a role in G protein selectivity consistent with the hypothesis that, in different G proteins, distinct domains of the Gα subunit could be responsible for receptor selectivity (Glukhova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence analysis and supported by citation to a hypothesis.

claim: No significant conformational changes of the β6-α5 loop happened before or during the GDP dissociation
source: Interestingly, no significant conformational changes of the β6-α5 loop happened before or during the GDP dissociation, suggesting that its conformational change as captured in the nucleotide-free GLP-1R:Gs complex (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) occurs after the GDP release as a result of the loss of binding stabilization, rather than being an initiator of the GDP dissociation.
evidence: This is an observation from the simulation trajectory and an inference about the sequence of events.

claim: mwSuMD is based on traditional SuMD while drawing on parallel multiple replica methods
source: To reduce some of these limits, we have developed and tested on complex structural events characterizing GPCRs, an energetically unbiased adaptive sampling algorithm, namely mwSuMD, which is based on traditional SuMD, while drawing on parallel multiple replica methods (Dickson and Brooks, 2014; Sugita and Okamoto, 1999).
evidence: This describes the methodological basis of mwSuMD with citations.

claim: Distance-driven mwSuMD obtained remarkable predictivity as demonstrated by the lowest deviation from the experimental AVP:V2R complex
source: Our simulations propose that remarkable predictivity can be obtained with distance-driven mwSuMD, as demonstrated by the lowest deviation from the experimental AVP:V2R complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the simulation results presented.

claim: The dissociation of AVP from V2R was simulated much more rapidly by mwSuMD than by SuMD
source: The dissociation of AVP from V2R was simulated much more rapidly by mwSuMD than by SuMD, suggesting it is an efficient tool for studying the dissociation of ligands from GPCRs.
evidence: This is a direct comparison of simulation times from the results.

claim: mwSuMD performed similarly to SuMD for the dynamic docking of AVP to V2R when time windows of 600 ps were employed
source: mwSuMD performed similarly to SuMD for the dynamic docking of AVP to V2R when time windows of 600 ps were employed.
evidence: This is a comparison of performance from the simulation results.

claim: Time windows of 100 ps remarkably improved mwSuMD performance for AVP binding to V2R
source: Time windows of 100 ps remarkably improved mwSuMD.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing different time window settings.

claim: The RMSD should be the metric of choice to study the binding path of well-known intermolecular complexes
source: The RMSD of AVP to the experimental coordinates as the supervised metric produced the best results. Consequently, the RMSD should be the metric of choice to study the binding path of well-known intermolecular complexes.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the simulation results.

claim: The distance is necessary when limited structural information about the binding mode is available
source: The distance, on the other hand, is necessary when limited structural information about the binding mode is available.
evidence: This is a methodological recommendation based on the nature of the metric.

claim: mwSuMD results suggest a concerted effect on GDP binding produced by AHD opening, αG-α4 loop rearrangement, and αG shift away from the GDP site
source: Our results suggest a concerted effect on GDP binding produced by AHD opening, αG-α4 loop rearrangement, and αG shift away from the GDP site.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the simulation results.

claim: The full rotation and elongation of α5 would occur after the GDP release
source: The full rotation and elongation of α5 as in cryo-EM structures would occur after the GDP release, supporting the role of hidden, metastable interactions as the driving force of G protein coupling and selectivity, as per recent work on GLP-1R (Yuan et al., 2023).
evidence: This is an inference from the simulation trajectory supported by citation.

claim: mwSuMD is designed to yield a mechanistic description of structural events
source: mwSuMD is designed to yield a mechanistic description of structural events.
evidence: This is a statement about the purpose and design of the method.

claim: mwSuMD trajectories can represent a backbone for further MD sampling aimed at quantifying or predicting the kinetics of the transition
source: We note that mwSuMD trajectories, since they describe the sequential states along a transition pathway, can represent a precious backbone for further MD sampling aimed at quantifying or predicting the kinetics of the transition.
evidence: This is a proposed application of the method.

claim: mwSuMD can be employed to study a wide range of structural phenomena characterizing both membrane and cytosolic proteins
source: Given the generality and simplicity of its implementation, we anticipate that mwSuMD can be employed to study a wide range of structural phenomena characterizing both membrane and cytosolic proteins.
evidence: This is a speculation about the broader applicability of the method.

claim: mwSuMD can exploit ACEMD, NAMD, GROMACS, and OPENMM as GPU-based MD engines
source: mwSuMD is an ongoing project updated on https://github.com/pipitoludovico/mwSuMD_multiEngine (copy archived at Pipitò, 2025) and, in the recent implementation, can exploit ACEMD (Harvey et al., 2009), NAMD (Phillips et al., 2005), GROMACS (Berendsen et al., 1995), and OPENMM (Eastman et al., 2017) as graphic processing units (GPU)-based MD engines while offering the option to run also on CPUs.
evidence: This is a description of the software implementation with citations.

claim: SuMD is an adaptive sampling method based on a tabu-like algorithm for speeding up the simulation of binding events without the introduction of any energetic bias
source: The SuMD is an adaptive sampling method (Deganutti and Moro, 2017) based on a tabu-like algorithm for speeding up the simulation of binding events between small molecules (or peptides [Salmaso et al., 2017; Bower et al., 2018]) and proteins (Cuzzolin et al., 2016; Sabbadin and Moro, 2014) without the introduction of any energetic bias.
evidence: This is a description of the SuMD method with citations.

claim: During SuMD, if the slope of distances is negative, the next simulation step starts from the last set of coordinates and velocities, otherwise the simulation is restarted by randomly assigning the atomic velocities
source: Briefly, during SuMD, a series of short unbiased MD simulations are performed, and after each simulation, the distances between the centers of mass (or the geometrical centers) of the ligand and the predicted binding site (collected at regular time intervals) are fitted to a linear function. If the resulting slope is negative (showing progress toward the target), the next simulation step starts from the last set of coordinates and velocities, otherwise, the simulation is restarted by randomly assigning the atomic velocities.
evidence: This is a description of the SuMD algorithm.

claim: mwSuMD is designed to increase the sampling from a specific configuration by seeding user-decided parallel replicas rather than one short simulation as per SuMD
source: mwSuMD is designed to increase the sampling from a specific configuration by seeding user-decided parallel replicas (walkers) rather than one short simulation as per SuMD.
evidence: This is a description of how mwSuMD differs from SuMD.

claim: One replica for each batch of walkers is always considered productive in mwSuMD
source: Since one replica for each batch of walkers is always considered productive, mwSuMD gives more control than SuMD on the total wall-clock time used for a simulation.
evidence: This is a description of the mwSuMD algorithm.

claim: To maximize mwSuMD, it is optimal to assign one walker per GPU
source: On the flip side, to maximize mwSuMD, it is optimal to assign one walker per GPU, requiring multiple GPUs to be effective.
evidence: This is a practical recommendation for implementing mwSuMD.

claim: The CHARMM36/CGenFF 3.0.1 force field combination was employed in this work
source: The CHARMM36 (Huang and MacKerell, 2013; Huang et al., 2017) /CGenFF 3.0.1 (Vanommeslaeghe and MacKerell, 2012; Vanommeslaeghe et al., 2012; Yu et al., 2012) force field combination was employed in this work.
evidence: This is a methodological detail with citations.

claim: The MD engine ACEMD3 was employed for both the equilibration and productive simulations
source: The MD engine ACEMD3 (Harvey et al., 2009) was employed for both the equilibration and productive simulations.
evidence: This is a methodological detail with citation.
